text:
The purchaser likely prevails because the easement was an easement appurtenant that was properly recorded and passed automatically with the dominant parcel—the house—when the man conveyed it to the purchaser by warranty deed. The brief unity of ownership did not extinguish the easement, and the purchaser's later discovery of it does not defeat his rights. Thus, the man's barricade wrongfully interfered with the purchaser's easement.
CONFIDENCE: 90
